reason: The sources contain more than 10 highly verified, multi-site claims to support an engaging story about our closest but invisible stellar neighbor.
story: Proxima Centauri is our solar system's closest stellar neighbor, located just 4.2 light-years away in the southern constellation Centaurus. Yet, this tiny red dwarf is so incredibly dim that it is completely invisible to the naked eye. While it has only about ten percent of our Sun's mass, its interior is fully convective, meaning it will slowly burn its fuel and outlive our Sun by shining for trillions of years. But don't expect a peaceful neighbor. Proxima Centauri is a highly active flare star, constantly erupting with violent outbursts. It hosts Proxima b, an Earth-sized planet in its habitable zone orbiting every 11.2 days. While liquid water could theoretically exist there, the star's ferocious magnetic activity and relentless flares threaten to strip away the planet's atmosphere entirely. This hostile cosmic neighbor proves that even the nearest worlds in our galaxy remain tantalizingly extreme.
angle: Our closest stellar neighbor, Proxima Centauri, is a tiny red dwarf that is completely invisible to the naked eye, yet it hosts an Earth-sized world being blasted by violent flares.

claims.claim: Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after our Sun.
Proxima Centauri is a small, low-mass red dwarf star.
Proxima Centauri is part of the Alpha Centauri star system.
It is located roughly 4.2 light-years away from the Sun.
It is too faint to be seen from Earth with the naked eye.
Proxima Centauri has a mass that is only about 10% to 12.5% of the Sun's mass.
The star's interior is fully convective, with plasma circulating throughout the entire body.
Due to internal fuel mixing and slow fusion, Proxima Centauri will shine for trillions of years.
Proxima Centauri is a flare star that experiences frequent, sudden increases in brightness.
It hosts an Earth-sized exoplanet named Proxima Centauri b.
Proxima Centauri b orbits within its host star's habitable zone where liquid water could exist.
Proxima b is located extremely close to its star, orbiting at a distance of about 7 million to 7.5 million kilometers.
Proxima b's orbital period around the star is approximately 11.2 Earth days.
Intense stellar flares and stellar winds from the star could strip away Proxima b's atmosphere.
Proxima Centauri has a candidate second planet named Proxima c, which is a super-Earth or gas dwarf orbiting farther out.
Proxima c has an estimated orbital period of approximately 1,900 days.
Proxima c orbits its star at a distance of approximately 1.5 AU.
The star has a third confirmed exoplanet named Proxima d, which is a sub-Earth.
Proxima Centauri has a regular cycle of magnetic activity that produces starspots over its surface.
Proxima Centauri is located in the southern constellation Centaurus.

disputed: The exact mass of Proxima b is reported differently, with some sources stating at least 1.06 times Earth's mass and others stating 1.3 times. A script should refer to it generally as Earth-sized or roughly Earth-mass.
The existence of the second planet Proxima c is unconfirmed or disputed. A script should treat it strictly as a candidate planet.
The exact distance to Proxima Centauri varies slightly between sources, ranging from 4.22 to 4.25 light-years. A script should use a rounded estimate like 4.2 light-years.
The star's rotation period has multiple conflicting measurements in studies, ranging from 83.5 to 116.6 days. A script should avoid claiming a precise rotation period.
